Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States of America, including Section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy 
Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)), and having determined that, 
upon the expiration of the period specified in the first proviso to Sectipn 
126a(2) of such Act and extended by Executive Orders No. 12193, 12295, and 
12351, failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European 
Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to the achievement 
of the United States non-proliferation objectives and would otherwise 
jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States, and having 
notified the Congress of this determination, I hereby extend the duration of 
that period to March 10,1984.
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
M arch  7, 1983.[FR Doc. 83-6225 
Filed 3-8-83; 10:08 am] 
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Determination under sec. 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act that failing to continue nuclear cooperation with EURATOM would be seriously prejudicial, and extension of the sec. 126a(2) period (already extended by EO 12193, 12295 and 12351) to March 10, 1984. Ended with the whole order: first end EO 12409, 1984-03-10. The order's only operative content is an extension of a statutory period to a fixed date, March 10, 1984; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. Later event attached: EO 12553 revocation (1986-02-25), which does not move the first end.

later_events.mechanism: formal revocation after the end: express revocation by EO 12553 ('it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:', followed by the table row 12409 'Extending the period for nuclear cooperation with EURATOM'); EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986); the extension had already run out on 1984-03-10, so this clears a spent order and does not move the first end

research_rationale: EO 12409 (signed 1983-03-07, 48 FR 9829), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence making a sec. 126a(2) determination and extending the period to March 10, 1984. The dossier's single clause (#whole, 'By the authority vested' through 'March 10,1984.') is the whole operative text; inventory confirmed without correction. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12409>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's only operative content is an extension of a statutory period to a fixed date, March 10, 1984; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. Held orders naming 12409 are EO 12463, 12506, 12553, 12554, 12587, 12629, 12670, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840, 12903 and 12955, each read in the relevant part: apart from EO 12553 they recite EO 12409 in the list of orders that extended the period and then extend it again by their own determination; none amends, suspends or revives EO 12409. EO 12463 (signed 1984-02-23, before the 1984-03-10 expiry) extends the period from March 10, 1984 to March 10, 1985 by its own determination; it does not say it amends or supersedes EO 12409, so EO 12409's extension ran its full term and EO 12463's took over at its end. The dossier's machine 'supersede' chain records from EO 12629, 12706, 12791, 12840 and 12903 are misattributions: each of those orders supersedes only its immediate predecessor (EO 12587, 12670, 12753, 12791 and 12840 respectively), not EO 12409, and all are after 1986. The dossier gaps 'target provision not located' for EO 12463, 12506, 12554 and 12753 are OFR 'See' cross-references, not events: their held texts contain no provision acting on EO 12409, only recitals, so they are closed as recitals, not left as material gaps. EO 12554 (1986-02-28) still recites EO 12409 three days after its revocation, which confirms the recital is history, not continuation. The EO 14252 hit is a file SHA-256 string. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is the 1984-03-10 expiry, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Same pattern as the probe's EO 12351 and the s4 EO 12193. Whether a recital in a later extension keeps an expired extension order alive is not asserted by any held source; the producer reads the recitals as history. Nothing relies on the pending report-deadline or transcription-as-copy rulings. First end: EO 12409, 1984-03-10. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12409 in full: it made one determination and extended a statutory period to 1984-03-10; cooperation with EURATOM during that year was a completed matter, and every later year rests on its own extension order. It created no office, fund, property or private right. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlived 1984-03-10. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

(held official FR text, 48 FR 15117), replacing EO 12358's own 'The Commission, shall terminate one year from this date.' (EO 12358, signed April 14, 1982, 47 FR 16311, held) before that date arrived. No held order extended the Commission beyond 1983-12-31: the only held texts naming EO 12358 or the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving are EO 12358, 12376, 12415 and 12553. The Commission terminated on 1983-12-31 under the date this order set, and the order's only content, continuing the Commission to that date, was exhausted then. EO 12553 later revoked the spent order (1986-02-25)

Navel Oranges Grown in Arizona and  
Designated Part of California;  
Limitation of Handling
AGENCY: Agricultural Marketing Service, 
USDA.
ACTION: Final rule.
SUMMARY: This regulation establishes 
the quantity of fresh Califomia-Arizona 
navel oranges that may be shipped to 
market during the period April 8-ApriI
14,1983. Such action is needed to 
provide for orderly marketing of fresh 
navel oranges for this period due to the 
marketing situation confronting the 
orange industry.
EFFECTIVE DATE: April 8,1983.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
William J. Doyle^ 202-447-5975.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Findings
This rule has been reviewed under 
USDA procedures and Executive Order 
12291 and has been designated a “non- 
major” rule. William T. Manley, Deputy 
Administrator, Agricultural Marketing 
Service, has certified that this action 
will not have a significant economic 
impact on a substantial number of small 
entities. This action is designed to 
promote orderly marketing of the 
Califomia-Arizona navel orange crop for 
the benefit of producers and will not 
substantially affect costs for the directly 
regulated handlers.
This regulation is issued under the 
marketing agreement, as amended, and 
Order No. 907, as amended (7 CFR Part 
907), regulating the handling of navel
oranges grown in Arizona and 
designated part of California. The 
agreement and order are effective under 
the Agricultural Marketing Agreement 
Act of 1937, as amended (7 U.S.C. 601- 
674). The action is based upon the 
recommendation and information 
submitted by the Navel Orange 
Administrative Committee and upon 
other available information. It is hereby 
iound that this action will tend to 
effectuate the declared policy of the Act.
This action is consistent with the 
marketing policy for 1982-83. The 
marketing policy was recommended by 
the committee following discussion at a 
public meeting on September 21,1982. 
The committee met again publicly on 
April 4,1983 at Bakersfield, California, 
to consider the current and prospective 
conditions of supply and demand and 
recommended a quantity of navel 
oranges deemed advisable to be 
handled during the specified week. The 
committee reports the demand for navel 
oranges is slower.
It is further found that it is 
impracticable and contrary to the public 
interest to give preliminary notice, 
engage in public rulemaking, and 
postpone the effective date until 30 days 
after publication in the Federal Register 
(5 U.S.C. 553), because of insufficient 
time between the date when information 
became available upon which this 
regulation is based and the effective 
date necessary to effectuate the 
declared policy of the Act. Interested 
persons were given an opportunity to 
submit information and views on the 
regulation at an open meeting. It is 
necessary to effectuate the declared 
policy of the Act to make this regulatory 
provision effective as specified, and 
handlers have been apprised of such 
provisions and the effective time.

research_rationale: EO 12415 (signed 1983-04-05, 48 FR 15117), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence amending Sec. 4(b) of EO 12358 to set the Commission's termination on December 31, 1983. The dossier's single clause (#whole, 'By the authority vested' through the closing quotation mark) is the whole operative text; the editorial note and the neighbouring Rules and Regulations pages are outside it. Inventory confirmed without correction. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12415>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's own words fix the Commission's termination on December 31, 1983; that is a termination date, not a report deadline (neither EO 12415 nor EO 12358 contains any reporting requirement). The by-number scan finds 12415 only in EO 12553 (the EO 14257 hit is a tariff heading number). EO 12376 (1982) amended EO 12358's membership sentence and does not touch Sec. 4(b); no held order after EO 12415 amends Sec. 4(b) again or extends the Commission. EO 12415's end rests on its own words, not on a whole-text restatement or on an event that does not name it, so the open owner method question raised in the probe does not arise here (it does arise for EO 12376, which is blocked). EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is 1983-12-31, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Same pattern as the probe's EO 12269 and EO 12351 (own dated term). The end source is the held official FR text, not the American Presidency Project transcriptions that the dossier's own-term leads cite, so nothing relies on the pending transcription-as-copy ruling, nor on the report-deadline ruling. First end: EO 12415, 1983-12-31. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12415 and EO 12358 in full: EO 12415 only reset the Commission's termination date; the Commission was an advisory body whose public-awareness and encouragement functions were completed activities with no legal force. EO 12415 created no office, fund, property or private right and transferred no function. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlived 1983-12-31. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

whole_order_end.mechanism: expiration of term: EO 12415 (sole operative sentence) amends Section 4(b) of EO 12358 to read 'The Commission shall terminate on December 31,1983.' (held official FR text, 48 FR 15117), replacing EO 12358's own 'The Commission, shall terminate one year from this date.' (EO 12358, signed April 14, 1982, 47 FR 16311, held) before that date arrived. No held order extended the Commission beyond 1983-12-31: the only held texts naming EO 12358 or the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving are EO 12358, 12376, 12415 and 12553. The Commission terminated on 1983-12-31 under the date this order set, and the order's only content, continuing the Commission to that date, was exhausted then. EO 12553 later revoked the spent order (1986-02-25)
